memo.verdict: Neutral; park; medium conviction at the Triaging stage. The record finds Subsea 7 a well-run deepwater installation contractor at the top of a supply-constrained cycle, fully priced at NOK 329.0 (2026-10-05): the change that built the case has run through all six layers of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain to the sell-side's estimates, and what remains on the modal path is a return of 5.4 percent a year over eighteen months and 1.8 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar. The case is parked on the return, not on the gate: no D or F sits on management (B), business quality (C), predictability (B) or trackability (B). Re-engage below about NOK 270 on the modal path (about NOK 251 under the drop-through sensitivity), or earlier if a record 2027 intake carries 2030 execution dates, or if the merger completes and the group holds 12x or better on a 25 percent segment margin; any of these would move the 'Modal return' to D or C and the 'Investment Thesis' to C. Turn bearish on the bear's re-run triggers: utilisation below 80 percent for two consecutive quarters; a write-down above USD 100m on one award; Brent sustained below USD 50.
case: - The external change is real, unusually strong for the industry, and mature. A fixed fleet of twenty high-specification rigid pipelay vessels met a multi-year rise in deepwater capital spending, and because a newbuild costs USD 750m to 900m with a 50 percent deposit and no yard slot, demand went into price, not capacity. Global offshore FID capital expenditure peaks around 2027 at USD 149bn (Rothschild & Co Redburn); subsea investment resilient through 2031, peaking around 2028 (Bernstein); deepwater breakevens USD 35 to 44 a barrel. Petrobras's 2026 to 2030 plan declines sharply after 2028; management expects a wind sanctioning lull to weaken Seaway 7 in 2028 and 2029; offshore exploration spending at a trough of 10 percent of total capital expenditure thins the pipeline behind. Demand KQ B (inflection happened 2023 to 2024, plateau now described); competition KQ B (three contractors, pricing for risk, direct awards; Allseas at Atapu 2 and TechnipFMC's 50 iEPCI awards keep it from A); own cycle KQ B (strong phase, improving in margin not volume); political and regulatory C (CADE clearance and stable Brazilian local content against the UK 78 percent marginal rate to March 2030 and the live EC and ACCC reviews); supply side C (two to three umbilical suppliers, tree lead times above 50 weeks, wage inflation 8 to 15 percent, mitigated by the 10 percent OneSubsea stake, back-to-back terms, indexation); macro C (FX losses USD 67m Q1 2026, 50m Q4 2025, 38m Q3 2025); disruption C (robotics threatens up to 40 percent of vessel-based work at the light end per one expert; heavy SURF insulated); catch-all C (the merger moves the stock from pure-play subsea to half of a group with onshore engineering, drilling and a USD 3.8bn Thai Oil arbitration).

- The internal change is a corporate event, not an operating change. Internal forces B: the screen's rule met with three strong forces (merger; guidance raised twice; returns stepped up to about NOK 33 a share for 2026) and an orderly succession; red flags absent (no caretaker, no PowerPoint transformation, no trivial raise, no crown jewels sold, net cash, no debt-funded buyback). Strategy change B (the merger articulated and resourced, not delivered); guidance raised A; shareholder returns A; price rises A (EPCI prices +3 to 5 percent a year in 2026 and 2027; PLSV rates near peak; against, Brazil per-well tender values declining and an expert's delivery margins guided down to 5 percent from 6.5 to 7.5 percent); acquisitions B (nil premium, complementary fleets, spoolbases Saipem lacks; integration unproven; the 2011 Acergy precedent delivered USD 100m of synergies within three years); standards B (selectivity, 2025 capex USD 281m below range, utilisation 87 percent); chief executive C (continuity, the same choices; Jefferies' small short-term negative); other leaders C; balance sheet C (used for distributions, not leverage); perimeter C; new geographies C; new products C (carbon capture about USD 80m, 1 percent of sales); catch-all C (one-off director fee on merger completion; Siem's under USD 1m legal costs reimbursed).

- 'Financial Outputs' have arrived rather than are arriving (C). Margin 15.9 percent 2024, 20.9 percent 2025, about 24 percent guided 2026; net debt to net cash; EPS roughly doubling in 2026; FY2027 consensus EPS +35.5 percent in twelve months. From here: our modal FY2026 to FY2028 EPS growth 5.3 percent a year; consensus +2.2 percent FY2027 and +4.9 percent FY2028. Goldilocks growth D: +85 to +95 percent in 2026 (above the 40 percent line the framework marks down hard), then about 5 percent a year to 2028 and about 2 percent to 2031; six months D (+73 percent H2 on H2; FY2026 +87 or +95 percent depending on basis), eighteen months D (the 24-month-forward figure from about NOK 26.1 to about NOK 28.2 at April 2028, +8.0 percent; FY2026 to FY2027 +8.9 percent), three years F (FY2026 to FY2029 +3.1 percent a year; the 24-month-forward figure NOK 26.1 to about NOK 27.5 at October 2029, +1.8 percent a year). Key metrics B: margin A (adjusted EBIT 3.2, 6.2, 10.7 percent 2023 to 2025; our modal 24.5 percent EBITDA margin 2027 to 2028 easing to 23.5 percent by 2030), cash conversion A (free cash flow USD -61m 2023, 372m 2024, 811m 2025, 197 percent of reported net income; company basis USD 1.2bn on operating cash flow USD 1,471m; against, contract liabilities +79 percent to USD 701m while unbilled receivables rose, a pattern the risks research calls inadequately reconciled), net debt A (1.39x at Q2 2024 to -0.12x at Q2 2026), revenue growth C (falling rate; Q1 2026 +17.0 and Q2 +9.8 percent lap +9.6 and +1.0 percent). Sell-side upgrades B: upgrade record A (initial guidance beaten 11 and 12 percent in consecutive years; ten consecutive quarterly beats; 2025 targets 18 to 21 percent; the 2022 Renewables misses the exception); guidance conservatism A (DNB Carnegie: consensus too conservative, 25 percent modelled against flattish about 24 percent; Bernstein: structural room for sequential beats; Rothschild & Co Redburn: the Vigra 18 to 20 percent ceiling shattered; against, Morgan Stanley's base case strictly at guidance, 23.2 percent 2027 to 2028); revision skew A (every post-results change a raise: Morgan Stanley +5 percent 2026 EBITDA; Rothschild & Co Redburn +11, +17, +9 percent EBITDA 2026 to 2028 and +27.8 percent FY2026 EPS); dashboard revisions B (next step most likely at the 19 November 2026 results if the H2 margin runs ahead of 24 percent); guidance versus consensus C (level); modal forecast C (our FY2026 EBITDA USD 1,875m, 24.2 percent on USD 7,750m, about 1 percent above the top of what guidance implies; our FY2026 EPS USD 2.71, 3 percent above the median; H2 EPS about USD 1.50 on H1 reported basic USD 1.197). Staircase B: near steps A (19 November 2026 results; EC by 26 November and ACCC by mid-November 2026; completion H2 2026 with the specials; CRPO-153 by end-2026; first combined guidance Q1 2027; AR7 FIDs), mid steps B (record 2027 intake expected; Petrobras nearly USD 10bn of awards and four PLSVs to 2028; Goliat Gas Export; Sakarya Phase 3; CRPO-148 mid-2027; OneSubsea USD 9bn of bookings over 24 months; first synergy reporting), far steps D (wind lull 2028 to 2029; Petrobras's 2029 decline; 2028 coverage 38 percent; against, EUR 300m synergy run-rate by 2029, AR7 and AR8 installations from 2029 to 2030).
counter_case: - The bull's case at full force: the market is still mis-pricing a structural change in the supply side of deepwater installation. Three contractors become two of consequence. Saipem7 would hold 40 percent of the world's rigid pipelay vessels and 60 to 65 percent of SURF; no newbuild can be ordered under USD 750m and three years; the standalone trades at a 9 to 10 percent free-cash-flow yield (consensus free cash flow USD 973m on a USD 9,872m market capitalisation) and the combined group at 5.4x EV/EBITDA against large-cap services at 10x; EUR 300m of synergies are not in the price; DNB Carnegie's 25 percent margin adds about 10 percent to FY2027 EPS; backlogs reaching 2030 to 2031 say the plateau is a floor, not a peak. On those premises 13 to 14x on about NOK 29 of earnings gives NOK 380 to 410 plus NOK 32 of cash by April 2028, 14 to 20 percent a year, and the sell-side targets of NOK 400 to 440 (DNB Carnegie, Rothschild & Co Redburn, Jefferies) say so. Low short interest reads as strong cycle conviction.

- What the record concedes: the structure (rated A); the cash yield, real and covering the ordinary dividend about twice; the record of ten quarters without a miss; that today's multiple is not a peak-cycle multiple; that the one quantified mis-modelling in the research, the margin line, runs in the bull's favour; and that if the merger completes and the market re-rates the group to 13x, the 'Modal return' is wrong by a full rating and the entry level is today's price. The branch the bull needs, completion then re-rating to 13x or better by April 2028, is put at about 28 percent (0.70 x 0.40): possible, not probable.
triggers: - The merger: EC Phase 2 decision by 26 November 2026; ACCC by mid-November 2026; completion probable (about 70 percent) in Q4 2026 to Q1 2027 on current terms. Alarm: an EC statement of objections requiring divestments. Invalidate: remedies above EUR 500m, a prohibition, or either party exercising the cancellation right. What would change the record's mind: a statement of objections naming vessel divestitures, or either party's words on the cancellation right.

- The margin: group and Subsea and Conventional adjusted EBITDA margin quarterly; our modal 24.2 percent FY2026, 24.5 percent FY2027 to FY2028, 23.5 percent by 2030; guidance about 24 percent; consensus 23.8 percent FY2026 to FY2027 and 23.5 percent FY2028. Alarm: group margin below 23 percent in any quarter. Invalidate: below 22 percent for two consecutive quarters. Upside trigger: the segment holding 25 percent or better, worth about 10 percent to FY2027 EPS.

- Cycle duration: awards and book-to-bill; backlog by execution year; Petrobras's plan; FIDs. Our modal: record 2027 intake, backlog above USD 13bn through 2027, revenue -2 percent a year in 2029 to 2030. Alarm: book-to-bill below 0.8x for two quarters or backlog below USD 12bn. Invalidate: Petrobras awarding more than three contracts outside the triopoly in twelve months, or Brent sustained below USD 50. What would change the record's mind upward: a record 2027 intake with 2030 execution dates, or a Petrobras plan revision upward.

- Lump-sum write-down: likely (about 80 percent) no provision above USD 100m in eighteen months. Alarm: any single-project provision above USD 50m. Invalidate: a write-down above USD 100m on one award.

- De-rating: 24-month-forward P/E against the five-year bands; our modal 11.5x at April 2028, 10.5x at October 2029. Alarm (confirming the modal): below 11.3x with earnings unchanged. Invalidate (the bull is right, the rating moves up): above 13.2x on a completed merger with earnings unchanged.
- Utilisation: 80 to 87 percent seasonally; alarm below 80 percent in a summer quarter; invalidate below 80 percent for two consecutive quarters, or attributed to integration.
